items.title: Identifying the Equation of a Line of Best Fit

sections.normalized_html:
The scatterplot shows the relationship between two variables, [MATH: x] and [MATH: y.] A line of best fit is also shown. Which of the following equations best represents the line of best fit?

  1. [MATH: y = 0.6x + 2.5]

  2. [MATH: y = -0.6x + 2.5]

  3. [MATH: y = 0.6x - 2.5]

  4. [MATH: y = -0.6x - 2.5]

sections.normalized_html:
We are asked to identify an equation that represents the line of best fit.

From the graph:

  • The line goes upward from left to right, so the slope is positive.

  • The line appears to cross the [MATH: y]-axis at approximately [MATH: 2.5,] so the [MATH: y]-intercept is [MATH: 2.5.]

Therefore, among the choices, the equation that best represents the line of best fit for the data points is [MATH: y = 0.6x + 2.5.]

sections.normalized_html:
The scatterplot above shows the impact of staffing on response time, where [MATH: k] is the number of support agents on shift and [MATH: r] is the average resolution time in minutes. A line of best fit is also shown. Which of the following could be an equation of the line of best fit shown?

  1. [MATH: r = 87.5 - 2.48\,k]

  2. [MATH: r = 87.5 + 2.48\,k]

  3. [MATH: r = -87.5 - 2.48\,k]

  4. [MATH: r = -87.5 + 2.48\,k]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/80976171efcfa4775cd6ef53c7725e1b]

The scatterplot above shows the impact of staffing on response time, where [MATH: k] is the number of support agents on shift and [MATH: r] is the average resolution time in minutes. A line of best fit is also shown. Which of the following could be an equation of the line of best fit shown?

1. [MATH: r = 87.5 - 2.48\,k]
2. [MATH: r = 87.5 + 2.48\,k]
3. [MATH: r = -87.5 - 2.48\,k]
4. [MATH: r = -87.5 + 2.48\,k]

sections.normalized_html:
We are asked to identify an equation that represents the line of best fit.

From the graph, we observe that:

  • The line slopes downward from left to right, decreasing by almost [MATH: 30] minutes in [MATH: r] for every [MATH: 12]-agent increase in [MATH: k.] That means [MATH: m=-\frac{30}{12}=-2.5.] Thus, the slope of the line of best fit should be slightly above [MATH: -2.5.]

  • The line crosses the [MATH: r]-axis at about [MATH: 90,] so a reasonable [MATH: r]-intercept is slightly below [MATH: 90.]

Therefore, among the choices, the model that best represents the line of best fit is [MATH: r = 87.5 - 2.48\,k.]

  1. [MATH: y = -3.3x + 36]

  2. [MATH: y = -3.3x - 36]

  3. [MATH: y = -3.3x + 28]

  4. [MATH: y = 3.3x + 36]

Each dot in the scatterplot above represents the weeks in physical therapy [MATH: x,] and the pain score [MATH: y,] in points, for each patient visit. The graph of which of the following equations is a line that most closely fits the data?

1. [MATH: y = -3.3x + 36]
2. [MATH: y = -3.3x - 36]
3. [MATH: y = -3.3x + 28]
4. [MATH: y = 3.3x + 36]

sections.normalized_html:
We are asked to identify the equation whose graph most closely represents the line of best fit for the data shown.

From the plot:

  • The data points appear to have a line of best fit with a positive [MATH: y]-intercept, so we can eliminate the choices with negative intercepts, namely [MATH: y = -3.3x - 36] and [MATH: y = 1.5x - 6.0.]

  • The data points slope downward from left to right, so the slope of the line of best fit should be negative, and we can accordingly eliminate the choice with a positive slope, namely [MATH: y = 3.3x + 36.]

Now, we are left with only two choices, [MATH: y = -3.3x + 36] and [MATH: y = -3.3x + 28.] Since the line of best fit appears to cross the [MATH: y]-axis near at a larger positive value (closer to [MATH: 36] than to [MATH: 28]), we eliminate [MATH: y = -3.3x + 28.] We can see that in the following graph.

Therefore, the most appropriate model for the line of best fit of the data shown is [MATH: y = -3.3x + 36.]
